headline: The US Energy Department has chosen four companies, three building small nuclear reactors and one making reactor fuel, for its new Nuclear Energy Launch Pad.
score_reason: Official announcement; early-stage support program with no stated funding.
importance_line: Small reactor developers get help with technical and regulatory steps, communities and data center operators may eventually gain new power options, and the article names no funding or timeline.
summary: The American Nuclear Society's Nuclear Newswire reports that the US Energy Department and its National Reactor Innovation Center announced the first four Nuclear Energy Launch Pad selections: microreactor developers Deployable Energy, NuCube Energy and Radiant Industries, and fuel supplier General Matter. Selection lets them start talks on technical, regulatory and deployment support; NRIC director Brad Tomer said the launch pad opens more pathways to deployment.
notes: Event date not stated; assumed new because published 15 Oct.
